subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this issue remain the canonical umbrella until the open cadence-guardrail and retention-cleanup PRs settle, or should maintainers split the remaining work into narrower issues now?
rationale: The source-backed bugs are real, but the permanent behavior spans compatibility-sensitive session cleanup and an operator-facing cron cadence policy that automation should not choose on its own.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Until Linked Slices Settle
options.body: Use this issue to track the combined user problem while reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89739 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only verified leftovers.

options.title: Split Remaining Work Now
options.body: Make the retention, cadence, context-warning, and sessions-cleanup pieces separate canonical issues and close this umbrella only after all context is linked forward.

options.title: Reject Core Cadence Guardrail
options.body: If maintainers do not want a core cron cadence policy, close or narrow that slice while keeping the retention bug path open.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Until Linked Slices Settle
recommendation.body: Use this issue to track the combined user problem while reviewing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89739 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90194, then split only verified leftovers.
